# duckdb-sqlalchemy

> SQLAlchemy dialect for DuckDB and MotherDuck. It supports SQLAlchemy Core and ORM (2.0 and 2.1), reflection, Alembic, pandas and Arrow, COPY helpers, and MotherDuck connection helpers. Install with `pip install duckdb-sqlalchemy`, import `duckdb_sqlalchemy`, and connect with `sqlalchemy.create_engine("duckdb:///...")`.

## Quick facts

- URLs: `duckdb:///:memory:`, `duckdb:///relative/file.duckdb`, `duckdb:////absolute/file.duckdb`, `duckdb:///md:my_db` (MotherDuck). Always three slashes before the database. A host, port, user or password in the URL raises `ArgumentError`.
- DuckDB settings go in the URL query (`?threads=4`) or `connect_args={"config": {...}}`. The URL wins.
- MotherDuck reads the token from the `MOTHERDUCK_TOKEN` (or `motherduck_token`) environment variable. Do not put tokens in URLs that are logged.
- Default pools: `SingletonThreadPool` for `:memory:` (one private database per thread), `QueuePool` for files and named `:memory:name` databases (shared across the process), `NullPool` for MotherDuck. Override with `poolclass=`.
- Compatibility: Python 3.10+. SQLAlchemy 2.0.0+ (2.0.45+ on Python 3.14, SQLAlchemy 2.1 needs Python 3.11+). DuckDB 1.3.0 to 1.5.x. DuckDB 2.0 is not supported. MotherDuck needs DuckDB 1.4.1 or newer.
- The package replaces `duckdb-engine`. Do not install both: each registers the `duckdb://` dialect.

## Public API

- `duckdb_sqlalchemy.URL(database=..., **config)` and `MotherDuckURL(database="md:...", **params)` build URLs.
- `create_motherduck_engine(database="md:...", ...)` and `create_engine_from_paths([...])` build engines.
- Table functions: `read_parquet`, `read_csv`, `read_csv_auto`, `table_function(name, *args, columns=...)`.
- Bulk helpers: `copy_from_parquet`, `copy_from_csv`, `copy_from_rows`, `copy_to_parquet`, `insert_from_arrow`.
- `checkpoint(connection)` runs CHECKPOINT with the commits it needs.
- Types in `duckdb_sqlalchemy.datatypes`: `Struct`, `Map`, `Union`, `FixedArray`, `HugeInteger`, `UBigInteger` and other DuckDB integer types.
- MotherDuck SQL functions: `md_create_dive`, `md_update_dive_content`, `md_list_dives`, `md_get_guide`, `md_create_flight`, `md_run_flight`, `prompt_jev` and related helpers.

## Execution options

- `duckdb_arrow=True`: SELECT results as Arrow (`result.arrow`, `result.batches()`).
- `duckdb_copy_threshold` (default 10000): row count at which an `executemany` INSERT loads through Arrow. `0` disables it.
- `duckdb_arraysize`: rows per `fetchmany()` with `stream_results=True`.
- `duckdb_retry_on_transient`, `duckdb_retry_count`, `duckdb_retry_backoff`: opt-in retries for idempotent statements.
- `create_engine(..., exact_decimal_division=True)`: exact DECIMAL division.

## Behavior to know before writing code

- DuckDB has no SAVEPOINT, so `begin_nested()` raises. `with_for_update()` is ignored.
- DuckDB cannot add UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY or CHECK constraints to an existing table. Alembic batch mode recreates the table.
- `result.rowcount` reports rows changed by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE. It is -1 with RETURNING and for `executemany`.
- `regexp_match` compiles to `regexp_matches()`, a substring match.
- Reflection without a schema covers the current database and schema. Pass `schema="db.schema"` for an attached database.
- Create a new `Inspector` after DDL. An `Inspector` caches the tables it resolved.
- Autoincrement integer primary keys use a sequence named `<table>_<column>_seq`, created and dropped with the table.
- Alembic needs no implementation class in `env.py`. The dialect registers `DuckDBImpl` when Alembic is loaded.

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/getting-started.html): install and first queries for local DuckDB and MotherDuck
- [Overview](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/overview.html): what the dialect provides
- [Connection URLs](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/connection-urls.html): URL formats, `URL` and `MotherDuckURL` helpers, escaping, pool overrides
- [Configuration](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/configuration.html): `connect_args`, extensions, filesystems, pool defaults, `checkpoint`
- [MotherDuck](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/motherduck.html): tokens, attach modes, reader pools, multiple writers, transient retry, supported DuckDB versions
- [MotherDuck Dives](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/dives.html): build and deploy Dives from Python
- [OLAP workflows](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/olap.html): table functions, Arrow results, streaming reads, COPY helpers, Parquet export, ATTACH, MotherDuck `md_*` functions
- [Pandas and Jupyter](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/pandas-jupyter.html): DataFrame registration and notebook use
- [Types and caveats](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/types-and-caveats.html): type mapping, execution options, reflection rules, unsupported and adapted statements, numeric precision, autoincrement
- [Performance and exact values](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/performance.html): bulk insert paths and when they fall back, Arrow ingestion, benchmarks
- [Alembic integration](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/alembic.html): migrations and batch mode
- [Migration from duckdb_engine](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/migration-from-duckdb-engine.html): switching packages
- [Breaking and behavior changes](https://leonardovida.github.io/duckdb-sqlalchemy/breaking-changes.html): every behavior change by version
